1264.17. Juli, apud Pyezka. — König Pfemysl Ottokar II. bestätigt die Be sitzungen des Stiftes Hohenfurt und nimmt dasselbe in seinen besonderen Schutz.

XV. In nomine sanete et indiuidue trinitatis amen. Otacharus dei gratia rex Boemorum dux Austrie et Styrie et marchio Moravie omnibus in perpetuum. Cum pia hominum studia pio fauore prin- cipum merito debeant roborari, maxime tamen id exigit ratio pietatis, cum elemosme largitati et bospitalitati religiosorumque profectui intenditur atque paci. Nos igitur deuocioni fidelis nostri Wockonis quondam marschalci regni nostri, qui pro suorum peccaminum remis- sione suorumque progenitorum uxoris sue atque heredum reme dio et salute monasterium Cysterciensis ordinis ¡n honorem glo riose uirginis dei genitricis fundauit, ex animo congaudentes ipsum monasterium in nostram recepimus protectionem et gratiam specia- lem cum omnibus prediis ac possessionibus*, quibus eundem locum dotauit et suo inseruit testamento, cuius tenorem presenti pagine de uerbo ad verbum duximus adnotandum: In nomine sanete etc. (Folgt nun die Urkunde Wok's von Rosenberg, ausgestellt zu Gratz * Folgt „eunde" durchgestrichen. 22 am 29. Mai 1261 (Nr. VIII), mit in der Note *) bemerkten Abwei chungen.) Volentes itaque domino complacere opera pietatis in aliis intendimus promnuere, que per nos uariis distractionibus impediti non sufficimus adimplere. Eapropter omnia hona memorato mona sterio a prefato fundatore collata, et quicquid ad presens possidet et in posterum donacioue fidelium uel propriis laboribus aut sumptibus iusto titulo possidebit, eidem perpetua stabilitate auctoritate nostre celsitudinis confirmamus ab omni uexacione et infestacione seu qua- libet uiolencia et iniuria ipsum regia munificencia contra maliuolen- ciam quorumlibet hominum eximentes. In cuius rei euidentiam pre- sentem paginam conscribi et sigilli nostri duplici fecimus munimine roborari. Data apud Pyezka. Anno domini M" CC° lxinj°xvi° Kalen. Augusti. Indictione vua. entries.english:
1264, 17 July, at Písek. King Přemysl Ottokar II confirms the possessions of the Hohenfurt monastery and takes it under his special protection.

XV. In the name of the holy and indivisible Trinity, amen. Ottokar, by the grace of God king of Bohemia, duke of Austria and Styria, and margrave of Moravia, to all for all time. Pious endeavors of men ought deservedly to be strengthened by the pious favor of princes; this is especially required by the reason of piety when one attends to almsgiving, hospitality, the advancement of religious persons, and peace. We therefore rejoice wholeheartedly in the devotion of our faithful Wok von Rosenberg, formerly marshal of our kingdom, who, for the remission of his sins and the remedy and salvation of his ancestors, his wife, and his heirs, founded a monastery of the Cistercian order in honor of the glorious Virgin, Mother of God. We have received that monastery into our protection and special favor, together with all estates and possessions with which he endowed that place and which he included in his testament. We have deemed it proper to set down the text of that testament here word for word: “In the name of the holy …” [The charter of Wok von Rosenberg, issued at Graz on 29 May 1261 (no. VIII), follows here, with the variants noted below.]

Wishing, therefore, to please the Lord, we intend to promote elsewhere works of piety which, occupied by various affairs, we cannot ourselves carry out. Accordingly, by the authority of our high office we confirm in perpetuity all goods bestowed upon the said monastery by the aforesaid founder, and whatever it now possesses or shall in future possess by the gift of the faithful, its own labor, or its own expense under lawful title. By our royal munificence we exempt it from every vexation, attack, violence, and injury, protecting it against the ill will of all people. To make this known, we have caused this document to be written and strengthened with the protection of our double seal. Given at Písek in the year of the Lord 1264, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of August, in the eighth indiction, in the third year of our reign. Issued by the hands of our protonotaries Peter and Ulrich.

1. A large seal, broken in two but otherwise well preserved, hangs from green-red silk cords and is made of white wax. Obverse: a knight riding at a gallop, whose shield bears a horizontal stripe. “Seal of Ottokar, by the grace of God king of Bohemia, and margrave of Moravia, duke of Austria and Styria.” Reverse: the king sits in full regalia on a throne, holding a scepter in his right hand and an orb in his left. “Seal of Ottokar, or Přemysl, fifth king of the Romans, margrave of Moravia, son of Wenceslas, the fourth king.” Compare no. XXI. 2. Millauer, p. 59, no. 8.

*) After “Nos igitur Wocko—marschalcus”—following the words “Bavariam dividentem” in the Hradisch charter—the following passage occurs: “Likewise, I will, order, and irrevocably decree that all villages situated on my estate between the Vltava and the bank of the smaller Vltava, and those that may in future be established there, shall belong to the parish church at Hohenfurt. Their inhabitants shall receive all ecclesiastical sacraments and render parish dues to the parish priest of that church, whoever he may be at the time; they shall hear divine offices from him, and the bodies of the deceased shall be buried in that church’s cemetery, as is fitting. They shall also give the priest one third of the tithes from all the fields they cultivate now or in future.” Then follows: “Likewise, on this side of the Vltava, beginning …” [The text lists Pzyn, Zwatemiri, Witigo of Krummau, the church at Rosental with its entire use, namely two parcels with their fields at Cedelitzrewt and one third of the tithes, then Mychenitz, full tithes from Predol and from the villages belonging to me and the aforesaid church, and from our manor at Polen, Gutenbrunn, Strobenitz, the village of Winthersdorf, Leutwenitz, Wernhardus, Sunneberch, Wezzel, Malchitz, Wernhardus, Wernhardus, Budiwoy, Liupoldus, and other names. “Item in Cedlixrevt—suis” is missing here. The title “Dominus” is missing before Habelo, Andreas, and Prehtlo; Prehtlo or Priehtlo appears without the addition “de Ried”; then follow Chvoradus de Tvrdelinge, Benada, Bvdylaus, and Graetz.]
